add.k: Wakanda's queen, mourning her son T'Challa
st: In season 1, Ramonda scoffs that N'Jobu sired no children, then backs Killmonger's plan and leads Wakanda's charge on the drones.

files.notes: Name not said in the episode; app names her Ramonda elsewhere (owner rule). The doubting line and the 'For T'Challa!' and 'Charge!' cries are hers per the wiki; transcript confirms the lines. The Dora Milaje are named on screen (Klaue's 'Dora Milaje spear', 'The Dora'll be here soon'), but the app files What If Wakandans under Wakanda and the story groups her as Wakanda's queen, so tm is Wakanda.

add.k: One of Justin Hammer's armed henchmen
st: In season 2, Sergei helps Justin Hammer seize Avengers Tower on Christmas Eve and chases Happy Hogan through it, guns firing.

files.notes: Name said on screen by Hammer ('Sergei, you stepped on my line, buddy'); lines 'Hey! Get back here.' Hammer's crew is never given a group name on screen, and he is a hired hand on one job, so tm is Independent. His fate after Hammer's defeat is not shown, so status is At large.

add.k: An Asgardian warrior in Loki's army
st: In season 1, Sif comes to Earth in Loki's army to avenge Thor and urges Loki to listen when Fury offers to find the killer.

files.notes: App names her Sif elsewhere (owner rule). Transcript tags her line 'Wait. He's not wrong. The All-Father would want us to listen.'

add.k: A general who brings tanks after Bruce Banner
st: In season 1, General Ross corners Natasha and Bruce Banner at Culver University and turns his guns on the Hulk, ignoring Betty.

files.notes: Natasha says 'I've got General Ross, a dozen snipers and a few tanks.' App names him Thaddeus Ross elsewhere, so n follows the owner rule. The Army is never named in this episode (only soldiers and tanks), so tm is Independent; reviewer may prefer U.S. Army. Wiki says he came to capture Natasha (wanted for murder).

add.k: A US general who blames Wakanda for Tony's death
st: In season 1, General Ross seizes Stark Industries, sends his drones into Wakanda, and readies the Jericho missiles after they fail.

files.notes: Only called 'General' on screen; app names him Thaddeus Ross elsewhere (owner rule). Group from his lines 'The U.S. Military is hereby seizing control of all Stark Industries assets' and 'Show them the true might of the U.S. Military.' Wiki calls it the Air Force, which is not said.

add.k: The Red Room handler of the Winter Soldier
st: In season 3, in 1991, Karpov sends the Winter Soldier after the serum, then tries the trigger words to make him kill Alexei.

files.notes: Dreykov says 'Da, Karpov' and the transcript tags his lines. Group: Alexei calls Karpov's no-extraction call 'Typical Red Room borscht' and Bucky says 'The Red Room just arrived. Karpov can flip my switch.' Wiki also lists Soviet Armed Forces and Hydra. Fate after the fight not shown.

add.k: A sorcerer fighting with the Alliance
st: In season 3, Wong holds a Vishanti protection spell so Riri can build her weapon, but dies in the attack, hidden by Beck's illusions.

files.notes: App names him Wong elsewhere (owner rule). Beck later reveals 'Your team is dead. The Alliance is dead'; scenes after Vision's defeat with Wong are illusions. Exact killer not shown (wiki says Mysterio).

add.k: An admiral leading the Alliance's last base
st: In season 3, Admiral Ying Nan recruits Riri to the Alliance and guards her lab, but dies in the attack, hidden by Beck's illusions.

files.notes: Says 'I'm Admiral Ying Nan with the Alliance.' Her later scenes (funeral speech, the raid on Beck's base) are Beck's illusions; Beck reveals the team is dead.

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Ramonda doubts Killmonger when he claims to be N'Jobu's son. She agrees to his plan against the American drones, fights beside him, and nods her approval after the victory.
stages.whoA: N'Jobu's son, who wins her trust
stages.whoB: T'Challa's mother, who comes to back him

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Ramonda and Shuri both doubt Killmonger when he arrives claiming to be N'Jobu's son. As the drones close in, Shuri still questions trusting him, and Ramonda leads Wakanda's charge.
stages.whoB: Her mother, who leads Wakanda's charge

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Sergei is part of the crew Justin Hammer leads into Avengers Tower on Christmas Eve. Hammer teases him for stepping on his line and sends his men after Happy Hogan.
stages.whoA: The boss behind the Christmas raid

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Happy Hogan tries to keep the Hulk blood from Hammer's crew. Sergei chases him through Avengers Tower, shooting at him, until Happy escapes.

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Sif comes to Earth in the army Loki leads to avenge Thor. When Fury asks for time, she tells Loki the All-Father would want them to listen, and he agrees.
stages.whoA: Thor's brother, who leads her army
stages.whoB: A warrior who urges him to listen

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Fury stands before Loki's army and asks for a chance to find Thor's killer. Sif backs him, telling Loki that Fury is not wrong.
stages.whoA: The director she tells Loki to hear out
stages.whoB: An Asgardian who backs his plea

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: General Ross surrounds Culver University with snipers and tanks while Natasha is wanted for murder. She tells him Bruce Banner is in her custody and to stand down, but the fight breaks out anyway.
stages.whoA: An agent who tells him to stand down

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: After Tony's death, Pepper doubts the story that Wakanda killed him. General Ross dismisses her, seizes Stark Industries under the Patriot Act, and tells her she works for him now.
stages.whoA: Tony's partner, forced to work for him
stages.whoB: The general who takes over her company

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Ross defends Killmonger when Pepper suspects him and praises the Liberator drones he helped build. Killmonger escorts the drones to Wakanda, then helps the Wakandans destroy them.
stages.whoB: The general who sends the drones

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Karpov wakes the Winter Soldier and sends him to steal the serum, then leaves him without extraction when he fails. Later he reads the trigger words to turn him on Alexei, but the soldier fights back.
stages.whoA: The Winter Soldier, who slips his control
stages.whoB: His handler, who holds the trigger words

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Karpov calls Dreykov, who tells him to defrost the Winter Soldier for a new mission. Later Karpov reminds the soldier that Dreykov warned him what failure would bring.
stages.whoA: His commander in the Red Room
stages.whoB: The handler who runs his Winter Soldier

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Alexei mocks the Red Room when Karpov cuts off their extraction. When Dreykov orders Alexei dead, Karpov tries to make the Winter Soldier do it.
stages.whoA: The Red Guardian he tries to have killed
stages.whoB: The handler who turns the Winter Soldier on him

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Wong and the Alliance save Riri and bring her to their base. He holds a protection spell against the attack while she builds her weapon against Vision, but he falls in the fight.
stages.whoB: A sorcerer who buys her time

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Wong and Admiral Ying Nan lead the last base of the Alliance. They hold off the attack on the lab together and both die, which Beck's illusions hide from Riri.

stages.title: What If...?
stages.text: Ying Nan saves Riri, introduces herself, and offers her everything she needs to build a weapon against Vision. She tells Riri to make some hope herself, then guards the lab and dies in the attack.

changes.was: T'Chaka welcomes Killmonger home as N'Jobu's son while Ramonda calls the claim foolishness. At the war council they both agree to let the American drones inside the shields.
changes.why: The app's only What If T'Chaka is the 1988 version (by-tchaka-1988, King T'Chaka on the 1988 team against Ego); no Killmonger's War T'Chaka file exists, so this tie would land on the wrong person.

changes.was: Ramonda and Okoye sit at the war council against the American drones. Ramonda leads the charge, and Okoye fights at her side until every drone falls.
changes.why: The app's only What If Okoye is the zombie-outbreak version (by-zombie-okoye); no Killmonger's War Okoye file exists, so this tie would land on the wrong person.

changes.was: Ross brings his troops to Culver University where Bruce is hiding. When a shot turns Bruce into the Hulk, Ross orders his men to take him down and fires at him himself.
changes.why: The app's What If Bruce Banners are the Mech Avengers version (by-bruce-mech) and the zombie version (by-zombie-bruce-banner); there is no file for the Avengers Assassinated Bruce, so this tie would land on the wrong person.

changes.was: Wong and Valkyrie fight side by side for the Alliance. They hold the base while Riri builds her weapon, and both die in the attack.
changes.why: The app's What If Valkyries are the Sakaar version (by-valkyrie-sakaar) and the zombie version (by-zombie-valkyrie); no Emergence Valkyrie file exists, so this tie would land on the wrong person.

changes.was: Admiral Ying Nan gives Captain Valkyrie her orders when they save Riri. They defend the Alliance base together and both die in the attack.
changes.why: The app's What If Valkyries are the Sakaar version (by-valkyrie-sakaar) and the zombie version (by-zombie-valkyrie); no Emergence Valkyrie file exists, so this tie would land on the wrong person.

changes.was: Ying Nan and Okoye lead the last of the Alliance and recruit Riri to their cause. Both die defending the base, a loss Beck's illusions hide.
changes.why: The app's only What If Okoye is the zombie-outbreak version (by-zombie-okoye); no Emergence Okoye file exists, so this tie would land on the wrong person.

changes.now: Ramonda and Shuri both doubt Killmonger when he arrives claiming to be N'Jobu's son. As the drones close in, Shuri still questions trusting him, and Ramonda leads Wakanda's charge.
changes.why: Important family tie missing: the wiki lists Shuri as Ramonda's daughter, Shuri (by-shuri-killmonger, in the app) is in the welcome scene ('What does he know of our people?' / 'These are my people too, cousin') and asks 'Are you certain about this, baba? Entrusting our fate to this outsider' before the shields open.
